questions.q: What are the three main killers in a station, as taught in the book?
options: The ticket queue, the stairs and the lights
The platform edge, the crowd, and fire
Noise, dust and delays
Lifts, shops and announcements
questions.explain: Station safety thinking starts with these three: platform edge, crowd and fire.

questions.q: Yellow-line discipline at a platform means:
options: Passengers stand on the yellow line for a better view
Only children follow the yellow line
Passengers wait behind the yellow line until the train stops and doors open
The line is purely decorative
questions.explain: The yellow line keeps passengers clear of the moving train and the platform edge until it is safe to board.

questions.q: How should a dangerous crowd surge at a station be managed?
options: Regulate entry at gates/concourse level before the platform becomes unsafe
Push more passengers onto the platform
Close the exits
Stop all announcements
questions.explain: Crowd control works upstream: hold people at concourse/gates so the platform never reaches a dangerous density.

questions.q: The gap between train and platform is mainly a risk of:
options: Ticket loss
Mobile network loss
Extra cleaning work
Passengers falling or getting trapped between the train and the platform
questions.explain: The train–platform gap is a classic interface risk, managed by alignment, announcements and staff vigilance.

questions.q: Door trapping risk is reduced by which features and procedure?
options: Painting doors yellow
Playing louder chimes
Obstruction detection, sensitive door edges and the re-open/re-close procedure
Locking doors permanently
questions.explain: If something is trapped, sensitive edges detect it and the operator re-opens and re-closes the doors safely.

questions.q: Platform Screen Door (PSD) discipline at a station means:
options: Platform Screen Doors are kept working and respected as the barrier between passengers and track
Passengers may lean on PSDs freely
PSDs can be blocked open for ventilation
PSDs are only for decoration
questions.explain: Platform Screen Doors (PSDs) are a safety barrier — they must function and be treated as the wall between platform and track.

questions.q: On hearing of an escalator emergency, staff should first:
options: Reverse the escalator at full speed
Ignore it until the crowd clears
Switch off station lights
Use the escalator emergency stop and assist passengers as per procedure
questions.explain: The emergency stop is there for exactly this moment; then help passengers and follow the station procedure.

questions.q: A passenger is stuck in a lift. Staff should follow:
options: Forcing the doors with any available tool at once
The lift rescue procedure, keeping the passenger informed and calm
Asking the passenger to climb out through the roof on their own
Waiting until the next day
questions.explain: Lift rescue is a laid-down procedure — communicate with the trapped passenger and rescue as prescribed.

questions.q: On a fire alarm in a station, the immediate priorities are:
options: Finish the current announcement first
Respond as per the fire procedure — alert, protect passengers and start evacuation if required
Lock the station exits
Hide the alarm from passengers
questions.explain: Fire alarm response is procedural: alert control, protect people, evacuate when required — escape routes must be clear.

questions.q: Why must evacuation routes and escape paths be kept clear at all times?
options: For inspection photographs
So cleaning is easier
So passengers and staff can escape quickly in a fire or emergency
They are not important
questions.explain: A blocked escape path turns an incident into a tragedy — no storage is allowed in escape routes.

questions.q: Which passengers get priority assistance in stations?
options: Divyangjan, elderly, children and sick passengers
Only season-ticket holders
Only passengers with luggage
Only staff relatives
questions.explain: Vulnerable passengers get priority help; staff are trained in first response and wheelchair/evacuation handling.

questions.q: Staff assisting a wheelchair user during an evacuation should be:
options: Any passer-by
Only the train operator
Nobody — wheelchair users wait alone
Trained in wheelchair and evacuation handling for Divyangjan passengers
questions.explain: Evacuating a Divyangjan passenger is a trained task, part of station staff's first-response skills.

questions.q: Operations Control Centre (OCC) maintains the 'safety picture'. This means Operations Control Centre (OCC):
options: Only watches Closed-Circuit Television (CCTV) for entertainment
Only announces train timings
Holds the overall view of safety across the network and authorises safety-critical actions
Works only during accidents
questions.explain: Operations Control Centre (OCC) authorises degraded working, possessions, isolations and emergency response — it owns the network safety picture.

questions.q: Which of these does Operations Control Centre (OCC) authorise?
options: Degraded working, possessions, power isolations (with power control) and service suspension/resumption
Staff leave applications
Canteen purchases
Advertising displays
questions.explain: Anything that changes the safety state of the railway goes through Operations Control Centre (OCC) authorisation.

questions.q: Every safety-critical Operations Control Centre (OCC) instruction must be:
options: Given casually and forgotten
Sent only by hand signal
Kept secret from stations
Logged with time, given in standard format and acknowledged by repeat-back
questions.explain: Time-stamped logging, standard format and repeat-back make Operations Control Centre (OCC) instructions traceable and error-proof.

questions.q: Operations Control Centre (OCC) must never issue an instruction that conflicts with an existing protection unless it first:
options: Asks the driver to be careful
Removes that protection formally
Writes it on a sticky note
Ignores the protection
questions.explain: Protections are removed formally, in order — never silently overridden by a new instruction.

questions.q: For critical Operations Control Centre (OCC) instructions, which verification practice is used?
options: One person guessing
Two-person verification before the instruction is executed
Passenger confirmation
No verification is needed
questions.explain: Two-person verification is a second pair of eyes on the instructions that can put trains and people together.

questions.q: Scenario: The platform is filling fast and the next train is 5 minutes away. Best station action:
options: Let everyone in to avoid complaints
Open the Platform Screen Doors (PSDs) early
Regulate entry at the concourse/gates and make announcements, keeping the platform edge safe
Ask passengers to stand closer to the edge
questions.explain: Control the crowd before the platform becomes unsafe — entry regulation is the prescribed tool.

questions.q: Scenario: A passenger's bag strap is trapped in the closed train door. The operator should:
options: Use the re-open/re-close procedure after checking obstruction detection indications
Depart immediately
Ask the passenger to pull harder while moving
Ignore the indication
questions.explain: Sensitive edges and obstruction detection exist for this; re-open, clear the obstruction, then close and check again.

questions.q: Scenario: An elderly passenger falls on the platform. Staff should:
options: Leave them until the train arrives
Only take a photograph for the report
Ask other passengers to carry them to a train
Give first response, assist the passenger and inform station control/Operations Control Centre (OCC) as per procedure
questions.explain: Station staff are trained in first response — help first, inform control, and record as required.

questions.q: Why is storage of material in escape paths strictly prohibited?
options: It looks untidy
It blocks advertisements
It can block evacuation and cost lives during a fire or emergency
It makes cleaning slower
questions.explain: Escape paths are life-safety equipment; storing anything in them defeats the evacuation plan.

questions.q: What is a 'crowd holding area' used for in station safety?
options: Holding passengers in a safe area so platform crowding stays within safe limits
Selling tickets
Parking staff vehicles
Storing cleaning material
questions.explain: Holding areas let staff meter the flow of passengers instead of letting the platform overfill.

questions.q: Which is an Operations Control Centre (OCC) safety duty during an emergency?
options: Cooking for the staff
Selling tickets at the station
Driving the rescue train personally in all cases
Authorising and coordinating the emergency response, including service suspension or resumption
questions.explain: Operations Control Centre (OCC) coordinates the response and decides suspension/resumption — that coordination is its safety role.

questions.q: Time-stamped logging of Operations Control Centre (OCC) instructions helps mainly because:
options: It makes the log book heavier
It creates an exact record of who instructed what, and when, for review and investigation
It replaces the need for repeat-back
It allows instructions to be given casually
questions.explain: The log is the memory of the control room — vital for learning and for any later enquiry.

questions.q: A passenger is found leaning against a Platform Screen Door (PSD), blocking its movement. Staff should:
options: Start the train anyway
Move the passenger away politely and check the Platform Screen Door (PSD) functions normally
Remove the PSD from service without informing anyone
Ignore it as harmless
questions.explain: Platform Screen Doors (PSDs) must be free to operate; staff intervene early and verify the door works before relying on it.

questions.q: Which combination makes the train–platform interface safer?
options: Louder music on the platform
More advertisements
Platform Screen Door (PSD) discipline, yellow-line discipline and door obstruction detection working together
Faster door closing
questions.explain: Interface safety is layered: screen doors, waiting discipline and sensitive door edges each cover a different failure.

questions.q: In a station fire, why are evacuation routes checked in advance during normal working?
options: Because a route found blocked during a fire is a route that fails when it is needed most
For exercise only
To complete a formality
They are never checked
questions.explain: Preparedness means the escape route is proved clear before the emergency, not discovered blocked during it.

questions.q: What should happen before Operations Control Centre (OCC) authorises resumption of normal service after an emergency at a station?
options: A fixed waiting time of one hour in all cases
The next shift taking over
Passengers asking for trains
Confirmation that the emergency is over and the station/section is safe for normal working
questions.explain: Resumption is a safety decision by Operations Control Centre (OCC) based on confirmation of safety, not on the clock or on pressure.

questions.q: Which staff action best protects a sick passenger on a platform?
options: Asking them to board any train quickly
Leaving them on a bench unattended
First response by trained staff, priority assistance and arranging medical help through control
Only giving them water and walking away
questions.explain: Sick passengers are a priority category — first response plus medical help arranged through control.

questions.q: The Operations Control Centre (OCC) instruction format being 'standard' mainly prevents:
options: Misunderstanding — everyone hears the same structure and can repeat it back exactly
The need for telephones
Delays in typing the log
Passengers hearing announcements
questions.explain: Standard format plus repeat-back is how safety-critical communication avoids the telephone-game error.

questions.q: Scenario: Two instructions exist — an old protection for a worksite and a new request to run a train through it. Operations Control Centre (OCC) should:
options: Authorise the train and hope the worksite is clear
Let the driver decide on arrival
Cancel the protection verbally later
Formally remove the protection first, in order, before authorising the train
questions.explain: An instruction conflicting with a protection can only follow the formal removal of that protection.

questions.q: Which is correct about escalator safety in stations?
options: Escalators need no emergency provision
Emergency stops must be known to staff and used immediately in an escalator emergency
Passengers operate all controls themselves
Escalators are switched off permanently
questions.explain: Staff must know and use the escalator emergency stop without hesitation when someone is in danger.

questions.q: Why do stations regulate entry instead of only controlling the platform?
options: To sell more tickets
Because once a platform is dangerously full, options are few — prevention at entry is safer
To keep the concourse busy
Entry regulation is not done
questions.explain: Crowd safety is won at the gate, not at the platform edge.

questions.q: A Divyangjan passenger needs to evacuate from a platform. The correct approach is:
options: The passenger is left until last with no plan
Other passengers are asked to carry the wheelchair down stairs without guidance
Trained staff assist using the wheelchair/evacuation handling procedure
The lift is used during a fire without checking procedure
questions.explain: Divyangjan evacuation is planned and performed by trained staff — it is part of station safety, not an afterthought.

questions.q: Operations Control Centre (OCC) logging, standard format and repeat-back together form part of which unit's subject as well?
options: Safety-critical communication and coordination
Ticketing
Catering
Advertising
questions.explain: These Operations Control Centre (OCC) practices are the safety-critical communication discipline examined across Units iii and vi.

questions.q: The yellow line painted along a platform edge is provided to:
options: Decorate the platform
Mark the safe standing distance — passengers must wait behind it, away from the platform edge and moving trains
Show where luggage should be kept
Indicate the coach positions only
questions.explain: The yellow line is a warning line: behind it, a passenger is clear of the train's dynamic envelope and of the platform-edge gap. Announcements and staff repeatedly pull passengers back behind this line.

questions.q: A passenger's hand is trapped in a closing train door and the train is about to start. The platform staff's immediate action is to:
options: Wave at the driver and hope he notices
Use the emergency stop facility / alert the train crew at once to prevent departure until the passenger is freed
Pull the passenger out by force while the train moves
Wait for the next station staff to act
questions.explain: A departing train with a trapped passenger can drag and kill. The emergency stop plunger/facility and an immediate alert to the crew exist exactly for this second-critical situation — departure must be prevented first, everything else after.

questions.q: On a confirmed fire in a station, passengers must be evacuated:
options: By the shortest route even if it passes through smoke
Along smoke-free, protected escape routes to a safe assembly point, while trains are stopped from entering the affected station
Only after the fire is fully extinguished
Through the track area in all cases
questions.explain: Smoke, not flame, kills most fire victims. Evacuation uses protected, smoke-free routes to an assembly point, and Operations Control Centre (OCC) stops trains from bringing more passengers into the affected station.

questions.q: An unattended bag is found on a platform. Station staff should:
options: Open it to check the contents
Not touch it, cordon the area, keep passengers away and inform Operations Control Centre (OCC) / security / police as per procedure
Throw it onto the track
Announce the owner's name and wait
questions.explain: An unattended bag is treated as a possible security threat until cleared by security agencies. Touching or moving it can trigger a device and destroys evidence — cordon, clear people away and escalate.

questions.q: A passenger has fallen onto the track at a station. Before anyone goes down to rescue him, it must be ensured that:
options: The next train is only a few minutes away
Train movements are stopped and traction power is isolated through Operations Control Centre (OCC) for that section
Passengers have finished filming
The passenger is conscious
questions.explain: A rescuer on a live track with live traction power becomes the second casualty. Movements are stopped and power isolated through Operations Control Centre (OCC) first — only then is the rescue attempted under protection.
